title: ED Raids 13 Sites in Probe Into Fraudulent NRI Housing Loans
excerpt: The Enforcement Directorate searched premises linked to Antriksh Promoters and Sunshine Infrawell across Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Chandigarh over housing loans allegedly obtained in NRIs' names with forged documents.
body:
• India's Enforcement Directorate searched 13 locations across Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Chandigarh on Friday, October 23, in a money-laundering case linked to allegedly fraudulent NRI housing loans obtained with forged documents, officials said.
  • The searches covered premises linked to Antriksh Promoters and Developers Pvt Ltd and Sunshine Infrawell Pvt Ltd, and were carried out under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
  • Officials have not stated the number or total value of the loans, whether arrests were made, or whether any property was attached, and the companies have not issued a response in the reports.
  • For readers: if you are an NRI buying or borrowing against property in India, verify every identity, income, ownership and authorisation document through the lender and developer directly — forged documents are the allegation at the center of this case.

India's Enforcement Directorate on Friday searched 13 locations across Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Chandigarh in a money-laundering investigation into housing loans allegedly obtained in the names of Non-Resident Indians using forged documents, officials said. The operation, reported by ANI and carried by The Hindu BusinessLine, began early in the morning and was conducted under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act in coordination with police and other security forces.

The premises covered were linked to Antriksh Promoters and Developers Pvt Ltd and Sunshine Infrawell Pvt Ltd, according to officials cited in the reports. Investigators said the aim was to gather evidence of the suspected financial irregularities and trace money linked to the alleged offence.

What Investigators Are Examining

The federal agency is examining the alleged role of the entities involved, the money trail and the total amount of the suspected fraud, officials said. During a search under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, the agency can provisionally seize documents and digital evidence believed to be proceeds of crime, subject to the provisions of the law.

Urban Acres, summarizing the same operation, noted what the initial reports do not establish: they did not specify the number or value of the loans under investigation, did not state whether arrests had been made or property attached, and did not include a response from either company. The searches across three city regions indicate investigators are examining records and possible financial links connected with the entities and the alleged loan transactions, the report said.

Why an NRI Loan Case Matters Across Borders

Housing loans for NRIs are, by design, remote transactions. The borrower lives outside India, income and identity documents travel across jurisdictions, and developers, brokers and lenders may each handle a different part of the file. Urban Acres noted that forged identity, income, ownership or authorisation documents can affect lenders, developers and buyers, and that investigations into the movement of funds can extend across multiple jurisdictions.

That structure makes document verification the central issue. If loans were drawn in NRIs' names on forged papers — the allegation officials described, not a finding — the people named could face loan records they did not create. That effect has not been reported in this case; it is the risk the evidence-gathering is meant to test.

For NRIs with an active housing loan or a purchase in progress in India, the practical step is direct verification: confirm the loan account, sanction letter and disbursement history with the lending institution through its official channels, confirm that any power of attorney or authorisation on file is one you actually executed, and keep your own copies of identity, income and ownership documents so a forged version can be challenged quickly if it surfaces.

What Is Not Yet Known

The amount at stake is the largest open question. Officials did not put a figure on the suspected fraud, and no agency statement quantifying the loans was included in Friday's coverage. The reports also do not name individual suspects beyond the two entities searched.

Searches are an evidence-gathering step, not a conviction or a final finding. Under the process described in the reports, the agency's next steps are to examine seized documents and digital evidence, trace the suspected money trail and determine the extent of the alleged irregularities, with any further action depending on what that examination finds.

What's Next

Expect the investigation to move from premises to paper: loan files, disbursement records and digital communications seized on Friday will determine whether the case expands to additional entities or individuals, and whether provisional attachment of property follows. For the diaspora, the case is a reminder to treat every India property transaction as a document audit — verify the lender, the developer and every authorisation in your name, because the allegation here is that the system was defeated at exactly that point.
